context: First, Songhai sat closer to the Hausa city-states of modern northern Nigeria and to the trans-Saharan caravan routes coming south from modern Algeria and Libya, which gave Songhai a different commercial orientation than Mali's western Bambuk-and-Bure gold focus.

The river supported a specialized fishing population — the **Sorko**, river-dwelling Songhai who lived in stilt villages and made their living from catfish, perch, and tilapia smoked and traded inland.
